text:
emily: Heads-up: a customer saw L4 choose the H100/FP16 fast-attn path and end-to-end token latency regressed 3-4x. Can we triage probe + fallback?
raj: Thats not expected. L4 lacks the WMMA/async-copy guarantees H100 provides. Do we capture the full probe result anywhere in logs?
marc: We only currently log a small tag (e.g., kernel_choice=fast_attn_v2) + device name. No detailed capability dump. That blind spot could explain it.
sara: I repro'd on a dev L4 box. The vendor query returned supports_tensor_ops=true, but a tiny microbench shows fast_attn is slower. Probe is too coarse.
emily: Current probe mixes model-dim heuristics + a vendor bit. We need explicit SM feature flags (warp-level FP16/WMMA, async-copy, shared-bank width).
raj: Proposal: probe surfaces explicit flags: sm_wmma_fp16, sm_async_copy, sm_shared_bankwidth_64, sm_tensor_core_version. If any required flag is missing -> do not select fast_attn.
devon: Also propose a microbenchmark during init: run 2-4 attention steps on a tiny buffer and compare to baseline. If microbench latency > baseline * 1.5 -> prefer generic kernel. Cost is ~5ms cold-start.
marc: Microbench is fine for Dedicated where cold-start budget is larger, but Hosted is multi-tenant so be conservative. Gate microbench behind probe_mode=aggressive for Dedicated; optional for Hosted.
sara: Agreed. For Hosted default keep probes cheap: explicit bitmask only + heuristics. But add runtime telemetry and an automatic watchdog to fallback when things go wrong.
emily: Watchdog idea: monitor token-level latency vs baseline. If p50 or p95 exceeds baseline * 2 for N requests or over a window T, switch kernels and emit telemetry.
raj: Sketch:
```
flags = query_sm_capabilities()
if flags.sm_wmma_fp16 and flags.sm_async_copy and flags.sm_shared_bankwidth_64:
    candidate = fast_attn
else:
    candidate = generic_attn
# runtime watchdog
if moving_avg(token_latency, 30s) > baseline * 2:
    switch_to(generic_attn)
    emit_telemetry(reason="watchdog_fallback")
```
marc: We need a versioned DeviceCapabilities schema. Current C++ device descriptor is ad-hoc. Add a versioned protobuf + a compat shim. For Hosted lightweight string bitflags okay to avoid churn.
devon: Rollout plan: Dedicated canaries first. 1% traffic in canary mode with probe_mode=aggressive + microbench. Compare p50/p95, token throughput, token cost. Also record kernel_switch_count to avoid flapping.
sara: Add cooldown after a kernel switch (e.g., 30s per model) and record kernel_switch_reason in logs. Also capture microbench_latency_ms and baseline_latency_ms in telemetry.
emily: Edge-case: quantized int8 kernels on L4 sometimes are faster but can change output distribution. Require model-level opt-in for int8 kernels and hook into evals before enabling.
raj: Add model_config fields: allow_int8_kernels:bool and kernel_sensitivity_test_id to map to eval harness runs.
marc: Telemetry fields to add: probe_flags, probe_mode, kernel_choice, microbench_latency_ms, baseline_latency_ms, kernel_switch_count, kernel_switch_reason.
emily: Storage: for Hosted use compact string bitflags; for Dedicated/Private persist full protobuf DeviceCapabilities. Migration path: compat shim that accepts older ad-hoc descriptors.
devon: QA checklist: reproduce on L4 with driver X.Y, run microbench, force vendor bit mismatch, validate watchdog triggers, run canary, verify no noisy switching and capture telemetry.
sara: Short-term mitigation: if vendor query is ambiguous about tensor support, force generic_attn for model dims > 2048 until probe is patched.
emac (bot): Deploy note: target runtime v1.12 for Dedicated canary next week. Tags: @eng-runtime @architecture @eng-sre
emily: Action items:
- raj: implement explicit probe flags + bitflag logging (PR)
- marc: add DeviceCapabilities protobuf + compat shim (PR)
- devon: microbench harness + gating config (PR)
- sara: telemetry fields + watchdog rules + cooldown (PR)
- emily: update rollout doc and canary plan
Any objections or additions?
